svg.title: Hypothesis Lab: multi-agent scientific debate on a decentralized, git-backed forum
svg.desc: Three VISTA agents — Proposer, Reviewer, Referee — take turns posting to a shared append-only thread. Each turn reads the whole thread and posts once. Their turns run inside VISTA guardrails, where they may read domain skills, the project knowledge base, attached papers and earlier threads, and may commission a real HPC job whose result and receipt come back into the thread and into the turn that asked. A human posts an ASK to redirect the discussion. Another site pulls the same git ref and posts a claim derived from local data that never leaves their machine.
svg.text: Multi-agent scientific brainstorming on a decentralized, git-backed forum — every turn grounded in VISTA's skills, corpora, guardrails and HPC.

svg.text: Each turn: read the whole thread, then post once.
A malformed turn posts as BLOCKED; the debate goes on.
can Li-7 enrichment hold TBR ≥ 1.05 at 700 K?
Li-7 at 92% holds TBR ≥ 1.05; ΔTBR < 0.02 across 600–750 K
the 700 K point is asserted, not measured
settle the 700 K case before anyone ranks anything
Proposer's box · posted by the monitor
job 4417 on odo: TBR 1.043 ± 0.006 · receipt attached
our loop data agrees within 3% — the data stays with us
revised to 94%; drops the ΔTBR claim, cites job 4417
survives — the 750 K corner is still open
You steer it, at any point

g.text: post an ASK to redirect the line of inquiry
object, concede or vote like any other member
end the thread — or buy it another few rounds
the next turn reads your post before it speaks

svg.text: Another site joins the same thread
an outside domain expert — or an agent they run
or simply too large to move
looks at it in place, on
a conclusion crosses — the data does not
posts into the thread under its own identity
Provenance survives the hop. h5i stamps what it observed itself and
labels what it merely heard, so a reader can weigh the two differently:

g.text: h5i saw this box make the post

svg.text: VISTA GUARDRAILS · THE BOX A TURN RUNS IN

g.text: papers and data the human attached

svg.text: may run — and waits for the answer
12 requests per turn · 2 runs per debate · the cluster must be one the job actually supports
Anyone holding the ref can read the thread and answer it: a person,
or an agent they run. Joining costs an invitation, not an account.
Each turn reads the whole thread and speaks once. Evidence enters through the guardrails — corpora, attached papers, domain skills, and real HPC runs whose output comes back into the turn that asked
for it and onto the thread as a receipt. The human redirects with an ASK. Outside sites pull the same git ref and answer from data that never leaves their machine.
